title: Enforce relay-policy rollout invariant and provenance-safe restore
scope: Backend projection durability, structured readiness evidence, deployment rollback gating, digest-pinned production images, source-version image metadata, signed backup export, cached-only restore, docs, and deterministic regressions. Settings UI components and stores are excluded.
intended_behavior: A rollout captures the pre-change relay-policy event ID, canonical payload hash, ordering timestamp, and projection health, then accepts the replacement only when readiness exposes the same valid policy or a canonically newer one.
Projection absence, regression, or a hash mismatch for the same policy event fails the deployment gate and restores the prior Compose configuration.
Production deployment inputs are immutable image digests, and backend and web images expose OCI source, revision, and version labels.

Backup export preserves the signed public relay-policy payload and event ID, payload hash, author, acceptance/event timestamps, schema, source relay, and sync timestamp without credentials or private keys.
Restore enters PostgreSQL only as cached last-known-good state and becomes relay-confirmed only after the same signed event or a canonically newer event is observed from a relay.
Restart or image replacement can hydrate cached last-known-good policy while the canonical relay is unavailable.
security: Projection mutation remains behind the signer-first approved ContextVM restore flow. Health evidence and backups contain only public signed policy provenance; source relay validation rejects credentials, query strings, and fragments.
